html:
Nelson's Dockyard at English Harbour, Antigua, was the main base of the British navy in the eastern Caribbean from the 1720s. Its deep, sheltered bay protected ships from hurricanes.

A young Horatio Nelson served there in the 1780s, enforcing the trade laws against American ships. The stone buildings were put up largely by enslaved Africans and kept the fleet ready in the wars with France.

The navy left in 1889. Restored from the 1950s, the dockyard became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016, and today it is a yachting centre. It is the only working Georgian naval dockyard left in the world, a relic of British sea power in the age of sail.
